sources.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina MFA: live visa nationality selector
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The official MFA selector is the controlling inbound nationality tool named by the research task, but independent trusted retrieval returned 502 and direct TLS verification reported an incomplete issuer chain; no certificate bypass was used.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Independent 2026-08-22 trusted retrieval returned 502 Bad Gateway.

sources.title: Decision on Visas
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: This Ministry-hosted Decision is the legal instrument identified by the Service for Foreigners Affairs as determining the visa-free nationality list, but it was not reproducible through trusted retrieval during this audit.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Independent 2026-08-22 retrieval returned 502; direct TLS verification failed.

sources.title: Law on Aliens
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: This is the Ministry-hosted legal source named by the research task, but trusted web retrieval returned 502 and direct replay reported an incomplete issuer chain; no bypass was used.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Independent 2026-08-22 trusted retrieval returned 502 Bad Gateway.

sources.title: FIPA: Visas and information for visitors
sources.publisher: Foreign Investment Promotion Agency of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: FIPA is published on the Council of Ministers domain and is an accessible government visitor summary, but its retained 2025 seasonal waiver note makes it unsuitable as a current replacement for the MFA selector.
sources.supportingExcerpt: From 01.06.2025. to 30 September 2025, citizens of Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Oman.

sources.title: Service for Foreigners Affairs: stay of aliens in BiH
sources.publisher: Service for Foreigners Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina
sources.officialityEvidence: The current competent Service guidance directly states that the Decision on Visas determines the countries whose citizens do not need a visa and identifies visa-free stay conditions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Decision on Visas determines the list of countries whose citizens do not need visas.

conflicts.explanation: The current state-agency schedule explicitly limits Hong Kong's exemption to a business passport. It does not establish the same route for an ordinary Hong Kong SAR passport, so the visa-free fallback is not promoted.

unresolved.reason: The controlling MFA nationality selector and Ministry-hosted Decision on Visas/Law materials could not be independently reopened through trusted retrieval on 2026-08-22: selector and PDFs returned 502 or timed out, while direct replay reported an incomplete TLS issuer chain. The accessible FIPA summary is not a safe substitute: it separately lists Hong Kong only under business passports, not an ordinary passport, and retains an expired 2025 seasonal waiver. The Service for Foreigners Affairs confirms that the Decision controls the visa-free list, but does not map an ordinary Hong Kong passport. No baseline is inferred from historic or outbound material, temporary waivers, exceptional border visas, or conditional Schengen/EU/US visa or residence substitutions.
